**PSR data shows 89% APP fraud reimbursement as losses climb back above £1.3 billion**

*UK banks reimbursed the vast majority of in-scope APP fraud claims in the scheme's first months, but total fraud losses rose 4% year on year, intensifying pressure on technology platforms to share the burden.*

New Payment Systems Regulator data reveals that 89% of in-scope authorised push payment fraud losses were reimbursed during the first 15 months of the mandatory reimbursement regime. That figure will reassure consumer advocates but confirms what many in the industry expected: the cost burden has landed squarely on payment firms while the upstream causes of fraud remain largely unaddressed.

UK Finance's annual fraud report, published alongside the PSR figures, puts total UK fraud losses at £1.28 billion for 2025, a 4% increase on the previous year. APP fraud drove the rise, rebounding sharply after a dip in 2024. The PSR has publicly called on technology firms, telecoms operators and banks to collaborate more effectively on prevention, and an independent review by Frontier Economics is due in early 2027.

The political dynamic is shifting. With banks now absorbing most reimbursement costs, the industry's argument that social media and messaging platforms should face binding obligations is gaining traction. Whether the forthcoming Frontier review recommends extending liability beyond payment firms will be the next inflection point.

*Sources: [APP fraud shifts focus beyond reimbursement](https://ibsintelligence.com/ibsi-news/app-fraud-shifts-focus-beyond-reimbursement/) — IBS Intelligence | [APP fraud back on the rise as crooks stole £1.3bn in 2025 - UK Finance](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47906/app-fraud-back-on-the-rise-as-crooks-stole-13bn-in-2025---uk-finance) — Finextra | [UK Banks Report Surge in APP Fraud Losses as Pressure Mounts on Meta and Tech Platforms](https://econotimes.com/UK-Banks-Report-Surge-in-APP-Fraud-Losses-as-Pressure-Mounts-on-Meta-and-Tech-Platforms-1744309) — EconoTimes*

**ACI Worldwide integrates Wero wallet, deepening its EPI infrastructure role**

*ACI Worldwide is embedding EPI's Wero digital wallet into its payments orchestration platform, extending its position in European instant payments infrastructure beyond clearing into merchant acceptance.*

ACI's partnership with EPI goes beyond the processing contract covered last week. The company will now integrate Wero directly into its orchestration layer, giving banks and merchants connected to ACI's platform a path to offer Wero as a payment method alongside cards and other instruments. In-store Wero acceptance through ACI is scheduled for 2027.

The move reflects ACI's strategy of positioning itself as a multi-rail orchestration layer rather than a single-scheme processor. For EPI, it is a distribution play: getting Wero onto the platforms that already serve a large share of European merchant acquiring and bank payment processing. The more orchestration platforms that carry Wero, the faster it can reach the merchant acceptance levels needed to compete with card networks.

ACI's share price rose over 6% on the announcement, suggesting the market sees the EPI relationship as material to revenue growth. The real test, however, is whether Wero can generate sufficient merchant transaction volume to justify the integration investment, something that remains unproven outside person-to-person payments.

*Sources: [ACI Worldwide joins EPI to integrate Wero wallet](https://thepaypers.com/payments/news/aci-worldwide-and-epi-partner-on-wero-instant-payments) — The Paypers | [ACI Worldwide and EPI to Power Instant Payments in Europe](https://financialit.net/news/payments/aci-worldwide-and-epi-power-instant-payments-europe) — Financial IT | [ACI Worldwide (ACIW) Is Up 6.3% After Joining EPI And Powering Wero Wallet Integration](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/aci-worldwide-aciw-6-3-160911292.html) — Yahoo Finance*

**China-backed mBridge cross-border payments platform set for commercial launch**

*The mBridge platform, built on distributed ledger technology and backed by the BIS and central banks such as the People's Bank of China, is moving to commercial operation, creating a potential alternative to correspondent banking for cross-border settlement.*

mBridge, the multi-central bank digital currency platform designed for cross-border payments, is preparing for its commercial launch, according to a Financial Times report. The platform enables participating central banks to settle cross-border transactions directly using their respective CBDCs, bypassing the correspondent banking network that currently underpins most international payments.

The project has been in development since 2021, initially under BIS Innovation Hub oversight, though the BIS stepped back from the project last year amid concerns about its geopolitical alignment. China's central role in the initiative has drawn scrutiny from Western policymakers who see mBridge as a potential channel for sanctions circumvention. The commercial launch will test whether those concerns translate into participation restrictions or whether pragmatic demand for cheaper, faster cross-border settlement overrides them.

For European payments professionals, mBridge matters as both a competitive signal and a policy question. If an alternative settlement infrastructure gains traction in Asia and the Middle East, it could fragment the global payments landscape in ways that affect European banks' correspondent banking revenues and complicate compliance frameworks.

*Sources: [China-led digital payments system mBridge set for commercial launch](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47920/china-led-digital-payments-system-mbridge-set-for-commercial-launch) — Finextra*

**Mexico's financial regulator pushes overhaul of fintech law covering open finance and crypto**

*Mexico's CNBV is pursuing a comprehensive rewrite of its fintech regulation, proposing tiered licensing, faster approvals and formal open finance rules in what would be one of Latin America's most ambitious regulatory updates.*

Mexico's National Banking and Securities Commission, under new chair Ángel Cabrera, is pushing for what the industry is calling 'Fintech 2', a broad reform of the 2018 Financial Technology Institutions Law. The proposed changes would introduce tiered, risk-based licensing to replace the current one-size-fits-all framework, establish formal open finance oversight and clarify rules around crypto assets.

The original law was a regional pioneer but has been criticised for slow licensing processes that have stifled growth. Industry groups are lobbying for the reforms to accelerate approval timelines while maintaining regulatory rigour. On open finance, Mexico would be following Brazil's lead in building a structured framework rather than relying on market-led API adoption.

European firms with Latin American operations or expansion plans should watch this closely. Mexico is the region's second-largest economy and a significant remittance corridor. A modernised regulatory framework could open new market entry paths for European payment providers and open banking platforms, particularly those already operating under PSD2-derived models that map reasonably well to tiered licensing regimes.

*Sources: [Mexico pushes to overhaul regulations for crypto and open finance](https://coinness.com/en/news/1160490) — CoinNess | [Mexico's Fintech Industry Pushes for 'Fintech 2' Reform Under New CNBV Chief Ángel Cabrera](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/334556586927602) — Binance | [Mexico's fintech sector advocates for reforms to the Financial Technology Law II](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/mexico-s-fintech-sector-pushes-for-financial-tech-2-bill-reforms-to-clarify-crypto-asset-regulations) — KuCoin*

**Euro Banking Association examines adoption criteria for tokenised money**

*The EBA's digital currencies working group has published the second part of its analysis on tokenised money adoption, identifying the practical criteria that will determine whether tokenised deposits and stablecoins gain traction in European wholesale and retail markets.*

The Euro Banking Association's Digital Currencies & Smart Payments Working Group has released an insight note examining the conditions under which tokenised forms of money, such as tokenised deposits, stablecoins and central bank digital currencies, could achieve meaningful adoption. The paper moves beyond theoretical frameworks to assess specific criteria such as interoperability, legal certainty, settlement finality and integration with existing payment infrastructures.

This is the second instalment in the EBA's tokenised money series. Where the first part mapped the landscape, this note focuses on what would need to be true for banks and payment providers to commit to building on tokenised rails. The working group draws on input from its member institutions, giving the analysis a practitioner perspective that pure policy papers often lack.

The timing is relevant given the ECB's ongoing digital euro preparations and the European Commission's work on the MiCA framework for stablecoins. As both regulatory tracks mature, the EBA's criteria could serve as a practical checklist for institutions evaluating whether and when to invest in tokenised money capabilities.

*Sources: [Euro Banking Association analyses drivers for adoption of tokenized money](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110135/euro-banking-association-analyses-drivers-for-adoption-of-tokenized-money) — Finextra*
